options.E: 少数发展为出血性胰腺炎

符合慢性胰腺炎的病变是

options.B: 腺泡及胰岛组织萎缩消失，伴有纤维化
options.C: 胰腺组织结构模糊不清
options.D: 胰腺周围脂肪钙皂形成

questions.title: 急性出血性胰腺炎的病变特点是

options.B: 腺泡及胰岛组织萎缩消失，伴有纤维化
options.D: 胰腺周围脂肪钙皂形成

questions.title: 符合急性胰腺炎病因发病的描述是

options.D: 由胰蛋白酶自身消化引起

不符合胰腺癌的描述是

options.B: CA19-9 是较好的肿瘤标记物

peptic ulcer
appendictis
fulminant hepatitis
portal cirrhosis

pancreatitis
hepatocellular carcinoma

After a long weekend of binge drinking, a 44-year-old man has a sudden onset of severe abdominal pain. On physical examination the pain is centered in the mid-epigastric region with radiation to the back, though there is marked diffuse tenderness in all quadrants. Bowel sounds are absent. No masses are palpable. Laboratory studies show his serum amylase and lipase are markedly increased. His symptoms become worse, and he passes away 2 days later. An autopsy is performed and the pancreas is shown above. Which of the following microscopic findings is most likely to be present in this patient?

A 72-year-old woman notes increasing jaundice and nausea for the past month. She reports 10 Kg weight loss during the past 5 months. On physical examination she is afebrile, but scleral icterus is present. There is no abdominal pain on palpation. She has active bowel sounds. A stool sample tested for occult blood is negative. Laboratory tests reveal normal levels of total protein and albumin, and increased levels of serum alkaline phosphatase, AST, ALT, total bilirubin, and direct bilirubin. Her serum level of CA19-9 antigen is also increased. Which of the following conditions is she most likely to have?

options.A: Carcinoma of the head of the pancreas
options.E: Colorectal carcinoma metastasizes to the liver

questions.title: A 50 year-old woman comes to her physician because of colicky right upper quadrant pain for the past week. She has nausea, but no vomiting or diarrhea. On physical examination, she is afebrile. There is marked tenderness in the right upper quadrant. The liver span is normal. An abdominal ultrasound scan shows calculi within the lumen of the gallbladder, and the gallbladder wall appears thickened. The patient's gallbladder is removed by laparoscopic cholecystectomy and has the appearance shown above. Which of the following mechanisms is most likely to have played a role in development of this disease?

options.E: Ingestion of foods rich in fat

questions.title: A 45-year-old man sees his physician because he has had nausea and colicky right upper quadrant pain for the past 2 days. On physical examination, his temperature is 38.7°C. No scleral icterus or generalized jaundice is noted. Laboratory studies show a WBC count of 10.5 × 10^9/L with 75% segmented neutrophils, 8% bands, 10% lymphocytes, and 7% monocytes. Serum levels of AST and ALT are within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.E: Acute perforation of a peptic ulcer

questions.title: A 44-year-old farmer from south China presents with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and is found to have ascites. CT scan reveals a nodular liver. Laboratory tests reveal increased levels of AST and ALT together with decreased levels of albumin and total protein. A liver biopsy is performed and findings are as shown above. Which of the follow-ing is the most likely cause of his disease?

A 18-year-old woman has had progressive malaise for the past year. She has become increasingly obtunded over the past week. On physical examination she is afebrile. On ocular examination, corneal Kayser-Fleischer rings are notices. Laboratory studies show increased level of plasma ammonia together with increased levels of serum total bilirubin, direct bilirubin, AST, and ALT. Her serum ceruloplasmin is high. The antimitochondrial antibody test is negative. A liver biopsy is performed. Which of the following microscopic findings is most likely to be present in this woman?

A previously healthy 38-year-old woman has had become increasingly obtunded. On physical examination, she has scleral icterus and her temperature is 38.9°C. Her blood pressure is 110/55 mmHg. Laboratory findings show a prolonged prothrombin time, elevated levels of serum ALT, AST, and ammonia and decreased levels of albumin and total protein. Her symptoms become worse with continuously increasing serum levels of liver enzymes and ammonia and dies within 2 weeks. An autopsy is performed and reveals a soft and shrunken liver. Which of the following microscopic changes of liver is most likely to be reported in this patient's report?

A 48-year-old man with fatigue is being evaluated for a 1 year history of elevated serum liver enzymes. A liver biopsy is taken and the pathology report for this specimen states there is grade 2 inflammatory activity with bridging necrosis and stage 1 fibrosis. The term "bridging necrosis" refers to which one of the following pathologic abnormalities?

options.A: Congo red-positive extracellular deposits surrounding necrotic hepatocytes in acinar zone
options.B: Destruction of the limiting plate with necrosis of hepatocytes surrounding the portal triad
options.C: Fibrosis around the central hepatic veins with apoptosis of adjacent hepatocytes
options.D: Necrosis of hepatocytes extending from the portal area of one hepatic lobule to the central vein of an adjacent lobule
options.E: Random necrosis of individual or small clusters of hepatocytes in acinar zone 3

questions.title: A 65-year-old man presents with increasing fatigue, weakness, anorexia, and jaundice over the past several months. Physical examination shows mild ascites and gynecomastia. CT scan shows a nodular liver. A liver biopsy reveals regenerative nodules of hepatocytes surrounded by fibrosis. Which of the following is the source of the excess collagen deposited in these fibrotic bands?

An epidemiologic study is conducted on patients infected with HBV in Singapore. These patients are followed for 10 years from the time of diagnosis. Historical data is collected to determine the mode of transmission of HBV. The patients receive periodic serologic testing for HBsAg, anti-HBs, and anti-HBc, as well as evaluation of serum for total bilirubin, AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, and prothrombin time. The study identifies a subset of patients who are positive for HBsAg and negative for anti-HBs antibody during the 10 year period of the study. However, these patients lack symptoms and have normal total serum bilirubin, AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, and albumin. Which of the following modes of transmission of HBV is most likely occurred in these patients?

A 53-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of marked hematemesis that has continued for the past 3 hours. On physical examination, he has a temperature of 35.9°C, pulse 112/min, respirations 26/min, and blood pressure 90/45 mmHg. He has a distended abdomen with a fluid wave, and the spleen tip is palpable. Which of the following diseases is most likely to be present in this patient?

A 45-year-old woman from south China experienced increasing malaise and 10 kg weight loss in the last year of her life. She became increasingly obtunded, lapsed into a coma, and died. At autopsy, the liver has the gross appearance shown above. Ingestion of which of the following is most likely to have played a role in the development of this condition?

A 51-year-old man has had increasing malaise and swelling of the lower legs for the past 4 months. On physical examination, he is afebrile and normotensive. There is pitting edema to the knees. The abdomen is slightly distended with a fluid wave, but there is no tenderness. The liver span is increased. Laboratory studies show decreased levels of total serum protein and albumin, increased serum levels of AST, ALT, and total bilirubin. A liver biopsy is performed, and the microscopic appearance of a trichrome stained specimen is shown above. Which of the following is most likely to have caused this illness?

A 53-year-old man has a long history of chronic hepatitis B and comes to the physician because of increasing malaise over the past year. He was hospitalized 1 year ago because of upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Physical examination reveals a firm nodular liver. Laboratory findings show a deceased level of serum albumin and prolonged prothrombin time. Which of the following additional physical examination findings is most likely to be present?

After experiencing malaise and increasing icterus for 6 weeks, a 42-year-old man sees his physician. Physical examination shows jaundice, but there are no other significant findings. Serologic test results are negative for IgM anti-HAV and anti-HCV, and positive for HBsAg. He receives treatment and is asked to come back 6 weeks later. Which of the following serologic test results can be used as a marker for recovery from this disease?

options.E: Positive Anti-HBc antibody and Anti-HBe antibody

questions.title: A study of patients who are infected with hepatitis virus A, B, C, D or E is conducted. The patients are categorized according to viral type of and are followed over the next 10 years. They receive periodic serologic testing to determine whether they are producing antibodies to the virus with which they were infected. Analysis of the data shows that a subset of patients progressed to chronic hepatitis and then to cirrhosis. In which of the following types of viral hepatitis are such conditions most likely to develop?

Ten years ago, a 32-year-old man saw a physician because he had experienced malaise, fever, and jaundice for 2 weeks. On physical examination there is mild right upper quadrant tenderness. Serologic test results are positive for HBsAg, HBV DNA, and IgG anti-HBc. The patient receives treatment and his symptoms are relieved but his serum transaminases are still abnormal after 6 months. During the following 7 years, the patients often felt fatigue and anorexia and was sent to an emergency department because of hematemesis and ascites. Serologic tests results were similar to those reported earlier. Sclerotherapy to treat esophageal varices was performed. Three years after this episode, he sees a physician because of a 5-kg weight loss, worsening abdominal pain, and rapid enlargement of the abdomen over the past month. Physical examination shows an increased liver span. Which of the following laboratory tests is most likely to be diagnostic of this last phase of his disease?

A 10-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of listlessness, malaise, and mild fever of 5 days duration. Dark urine is observed by one of the caregivers. On physical examination, there is mild scleral icterus and mild right upper quadrant tenderness. Laboratory studies show increased levels of AST, ALT, total bilirubin and direct bilirubin, but total protein and albumin are within normal limits. Serologic tests are positive for anti-HBs, anti-HBc, IgM anti-HAV, and IgG anti-HAV, but negative for HBsAg, IgM anti-HBc, anti HCV and anti HDV. Based on these findings, which of the following is true?

options.A: He now has an acute HAV infection
options.B: He now has an acute HBV infection
options.C: He inow has a chronic HAV infection
options.D: He inow has a chronic HBV infection

questions.title: A 48-year-old Chinese man has noticed increasing abdominal girth and a yellowish color to his skin over the past 5 months. On physical examination, he has scleral icterus and generalized jaundice. His abdomen is distended, and a fluid wave is present. Laboratory studies include markedly elevated total serum bilirubin, direct bilirubin, AST, ALT, and a decreased albumin level. The prothrombin time is prolonged. The blood ammonia level is also elevated. No mass is noted with ultrasound scan. Serologic tests are performed. Which of the following is the most likely serologic finding in this patient?

A 41-year-old man is found in an obtunded state and taken to the hospital. On admission physical examination shows he is icteric. His abdomen is enlarged with a fluid wave. An abdominal CT scan shows extensive intraperitoneal fluid and a uniformly enlarged liver. Laboratory studies show slightly decreased total protein and albumin, and obviously elevated serum levels of total bilirubin, AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase and ammonia. Serologic test results are negative for HBs Ag, IgM anti-HAV, anti-HBs, anti-HBc and anti-HCV. A liver biopsy is performed which shows abundant Mallory's hyaline, neutrophilic infiltrates, necrosis of hepatocytes, and extensive macrovesicular steatosis. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these changes?

A 54-year-old man has had malaise with a 10 kg weight loss over the past 6 months. On physical examination he has a firm, nodular liver edge. His stool is negative for occult blood. Laboratory studies are positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, but serologies for hepatitis B surface antibody, hepatitis A IgM antibody, and hepatitis C antibody are negative. His serum alpha-fetoprotein is 109 ng/mL. Which of the following abnormalities is the patient not likely to have?

A 40-year-old man has a 20-year history of chronic alcohol abuse. On physical examination his liver edge is firm on palpation of the abdomen, but the liver does not appear to be enlarged. An abdominal CT scan reveals that the liver has cirrhosis. Which of the following consequences is the patient most likely to be at risk for?

A 42-year-old man has had a fever and a productive cough for the past 3 days. On physical examination there is dullness to percussion over the right upper lung. His temperature is 37.9 C. A chest radiograph reveals right upper lobe consolidation. Laboratory findings show a slightly decreased level of serum total protein and albumin, increased levels of AST and ALT, and a prolonged prothrombin time. He does not respond to antibiotic therapy and dies. He is found at autopsy to have an enlarged liver that microscopically shows most of the hepatocytes to be filled with large lipid droplets. Which of the following histologic changes is most likely also present in this specimen?

options.B: Prominent lymphoid aggregates in the portal tract

questions.title: A group of undergraduate students plan to donate blood. Among them, a 20-year-old girl is found to be positive for HBsAg and is therefore excluded as a blood donor. Further work-up reveals no significant physical examination findings. Laboratory values for total serum bilirubin, AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, and albumin are normal. Serologic test results are negative for IgM anti-HAV, anti-HBc, and anti-HCV. Repeat testing 6 months later yields the same results. Which of the following is true for this patient?

options.A: She acquired this infection through intravenous drug use
options.B: She acquired this infection from enteric transmission
options.C: She will soon develop chronic hepatitis
options.D: This is probably a chronic carrier state
options.E: She should get a hepatitis B vaccination series

questions.title: A 41-year-old woman has had increasing malaise and nausea for the past 2 weeks. On physical examination, she has icterus and mild right upper quadrant tenderness. A scar is noted on the left upper quadrant. The patient reports that she had her spleen removed 2 years ago following a traffic accident. Laboratory studies show increased levels of serum AST and ALT, as well as increased total and direct bilirubin. She continues to have malaise for the next year. A liver biopsy is performed. The specimen shows spotty necrosis, mild steatosis of hepatocytes, and lymphoid aggregates in the portal tract. An infection with which of the following viruses is most likely to produce these findings?

A 12-year-old boy presents with malaise, fatigue, and loss of appetite for 4 days. His mother reports that he has had a meal with fried river snail at lake side 3 weeks ago. On physical examination, he has mild scleral icterus. Laboratory studies show slightly elevated serum AST and ALT. The total bilirubin concentration and the direct bilirubin concentration are also increased. His symptoms gradually subside over the next 3 weeks. Which of the following serologic test results is most likely to be positive in this patient?

A 56-year-old man from Henan province has experienced fatigue and a 15-kg weight loss over the past 5 months. Physical examination yields no remarkable findings. Laboratory test results are positive for HBsAg and negative for anti-HCV and anti-HAV and there is an increased level of serum alpha fetoprotein. An abdominal CT scan shows a 10-cm solid mass in the left lobe of the liver which is nodular. A liver biopsy of the lesion is performed and shown above. Which of the following is not true for this patient?

options.A: The mass is a primary hepatocellular carcinoma
options.B: The mass developed in the setting of cirrhosis
options.C: High fat diet is an accelator for the development of this mass
options.D: Repeated cycles of liver cell necrosis and regeneration caused by HBV is the mechanism for the development of the mass

questions.title: To your knowledge, for patients known to be infected with various forms of infectious hepatitis, which of the following is the best predictor for the development of chronic liver disease and progression to cirrhosis?

options.A: Type of the infected hepatitis virus
options.B: Degree of transaminase enzymes are increased
options.C: Length of time that transaminase enzymes remain elevated
options.D: Presence of chronic inflammatory cells in the portal tract
options.E: Presence of chronic inflammatory cells in the sinusoids

questions.title: A 44-year-old man has been feeling fatigued for the past 4 months. He remembers that he had jaundice about 10 years ago, but that resolved 2 months later and he has been healthy since. On physical examination there are no remarkable findings. Laboratory studies show his hemoglobin is 14.0 g/dL. A chemistry panel reveals normal serum electrolytes, but he has a decreased level of total protein and albumin, an increased level of ALT and AST, as well as a slightly elevated level of total bilirubin and direct bilirubin. A liver biopsy is performed and microscopic examination shows disruption of the limiting plate of hepatocytes with extension of inflammation into the lobules from the triads. There is focal ballooning degeneration of hepatocytes. Which of the following laboratory test findings is most characteristic of his disease?

A 30-year-old man has had nausea and vague epigastric abdominal pain for the past 24 hours, but now the pain has become more severe and localized to right lower abdomen. On physical examination, his temperature is 38.5°C. There is haphalgesia and rebound tenderness in the right lower quadrant. An appendectomy is performed. On gross examination, the serosal surface of appendix is congested and is covered by exudate. The appendix wall is slightly thickened at the base and the lumen is filled with pus but no fecalith is noted. Microscopically, the mass is composed of nests of cells with uniform small round nuclei and cytoplasm with small purple granules. The cytoplasm is positive with antibody to chromogranin on immunohistochemical staining. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.E: Acute appendicitis secondary to carcinoid tumor

questions.title: A 25-year-old man has had nausea and vague epigastric abdominal pain for the past 2 days, but now the pain is localizing to the right lower quadrant. His temperature is 38.7°C. On palpation, there is diffuse abdominal tenderness and rebound tenderness. Paracentesis yields 300mL of cloudy yellow fluid. A Gram stain of the fluid shows gram-negative rods. An emergency surgery is performed and the appendix is removed. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old woman has had nausea and vague epigastric abdominal pain for the past 24 hours, but now the pain has become more severe and localized to right lower abdomen. On physical examination, her temperature is 38.5°C. There is haphalgesia and rebound tenderness in the right lower quadrant. A stool sample is negative for occult blood. Abdominal plain film radiographs show no free air. The result of a serum pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following laboratory findings is most likely present in this patient?

options.E: Clostridium difficile toxin in stool sample

questions.title: A 53-year-old woman has been feeling increasingly tired for 3 months. She has had vague abdomimal pain for the past month. On physical examination, her stool is positive for occult blood. Abnormal laboratory findings include an elevated CEA level. Colonoscopy is performed and biopsy is taken from a 4 cm ulcerative mass in the cecum. The microscopic features are shown above. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman has had increasing abdominal distention for the past 6 weeks. On physical examination, there is an abdominal fluid wave and bowel sounds are present. Paracentesis yields 1000mL of slightly cloudy serous fluid. Cytologic examination of the fluid shows malignant cells consistent with adenocarcinoma. Further workup reveals a 7 cm circumferential mass in the transverse colon. Which of the following conditions has most likely occurred in this patient?

options.D: Local spreads of colon adenocarcinoma to the serosal surface

questions.title: A 53-year-old woman saw her physician because she felt increasingly tired and listless over the past 5 months. On physical examination, there were no remarkable findings except for a positive result on stool guaiac testing. Laboratory tests showed an elevated CEA level. Colonoscopy was performed, followed by partial colectomy. After this operation, the CEA level decreased back to a normal level. The patient refused further treatment. Three years latter, in a follow-up study, it is noted that the serum CEA level of the patient is elevated again. An ultrasound scan reveals two masses in the liver of 3 and 5 cm in greatest dimension. Which of the following conditions has most likely occurred in this patient?

options.C: Implantation metastasis of colon adenocarcinoma to the liver
options.D: Heterochronic carcinoma of colon and liver

questions.title: A 70-year-old man sees his physician for change in bowel habits. On physical examination, there are no remarkable findings. A colonoscopy is performed and shows a 5-cm sessile mass in the upper portion of the descending colon. The histologic examination of a biopsy specimen from the lesion confirms it is a benign neoplasm with villiform structure and moderate to severe epithelial dysplasia. The patient refuses further workup and treatment. Five years later, he is see in the emergency room because of intestinal obstruction. On surgical exploration, there is a 7 cm mass encircling the descending colon and multiple enlarged lymph nodes are detected in the mesentery. Which of the following neoplasms is he now most likely to have?

A 19-year-old man is advised to see his physician because genetic screening has detected a disease in other family members. On physical examination, a stool sample is positive for occult blood. A colonoscopy is performed, followed by a colectomy. The gross appearance of the mucosal surface of the colectomy specimen is shown above. Which of the following genetic changes is the patient most likely to have?

options.D: Defection of DNA mismatch repair genes

questions.title: A 45-year-old man has a routine health maintenance examination. A stool sample is positive for occult blood. On colonoscopy, an ulcerative lesion is seen projecting into the cecum. The microscopic appearance of a section of the excised lesion is shown in the figure above. Which of the following molecular biologic events is thought to be most critical in the development of such lesions?

options.C: Germ-line transmission of a defective RB gene
options.E: Germ-line transmission of a defective APC gene

questions.title: A 55-year-old man has a routine health maintenance examination. Physical examination is unremarkable except that the stool sample is positive for occult blood. Colonoscopy is performed and a 1.5 cm pedunculated polyp with erosion is noted in the sigmoid colon. Microscopic examination reveals a tubulovillous adenoma. Which of the following is not true?

options.A: This is a precurosor lesion of colon cancer
options.B: High fat diet is a risk factor
options.D: Colonoscopy should be performed on his family members to exclude colon cancer
options.E: It is more common in the left-side colon than that in right-side colon

questions.title: A 20-year-old man is healthy but has a family history of colon cancer at a young age. There are no abnormal physical examination findings. He undergoes colonoscopy and there are countless polyps ranging in size from 0.2 to 1 cm. A representative microscopic picture of these polyps is shown above. Which of the following diseases is he most likely to have?

A 57-year-old woman comes to her physician for a routine health maintenance examination. The only abnormal finding is a stool specimen that contains occult blood. Colonoscopy shows two polyps, one is in the descending colon and is less than 0.5 cm in diameter with a smooth surface. The other is in the sigmoid colon, 1.5-cm in diameter with a 0.5-cm stalk. The polyp is removed, and its histology shows a gland-forming neoplasm with severe epithelial dysplasia. There is no evidence that the tumor has extended beyond the muscularis mucosa. When the physician discusses these findings with the patient, which of the following statements is most appropriate?

options.A: You have genomic mutation of the APC gene
options.B: Your family members are in great risk of developing colon cancer
options.C: You will develop many polyps within the next few years
options.D: You are in great risk of developing endometrial cancer
options.E: You need not to have additional examination to look for metastases from this lesion

questions.title: A 70-year-old previously healthy man sees his physician for blood streaked stool. Physical examination is unremarkable. His stool is positive for blood but no lesion is palpated on digital rectal examination. There is no tenderness and bowel sounds are active. A cholecystectomy scar is present in the right upper quadrant. A colonoscopy is performed. About 20 cm above the anal verge， there is a 4.5 cm mass with superficial ulceration protruding into the lumen. Which of the following risk factors was most likely to have been present for development of this lesion?

A 45-year-old man has had recurrent low volume, bloody, mucoid diarrhea for 13 years accompanied by lower abdominal pain. Physical examination only reveals mild diffuse lower abdominal tenderness but no masses. His stool is positive for occult blood. Colonoscopy reveals erythematous, friable colonic mucosa extending from the rectum to the splenic flexure with formation of pseudopolyps. Colonic biopsies reveal mucosal ulceration with crypt abscesses and low grade dysplasia. Which of the following complications is he most likely to develop?

A 62-year-old man comes to his physician because of rectal bleeding. No other symptoms are present. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory tests show an elevated CEA level. Colonoscopy is performed and there is a 3 cm ulcerative mass which occupies up to 3/4 of the colonic wall. The mass is resected and the gross findings are as shown above. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man is having a routine physical examination because of a history of colon cancer in his family. He has no symptoms and physical examination is unremarkable. A laboratory study shows his stool is positive for occult blood. Colonoscopy is performed. Six polyps are found in the ascending and transverse colon. Two of them are pedunculated tubular adenomas less than 0.5 cm in diameter, three are 1 cm tubulovillous adenomas, and one is a 2.5 cm sessile villous adenoma in the ascending colon containing a focus of well differentiated adenocarcinoma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.C: Adenocarcinoma arising in a background of chronic ulcerative colitis
options.D: Adenocarcinoma arising in a background of familial adenomatous polyposis

questions.title: A 27-year-old man presents with intermittent cramping abdominal pain and low-volume diarrhea for several weeks. On physical examination, he is afebrile, and there is mild lower abdominal tenderness but no masses, and bowel sounds are present. A stool sample is positive for occult blood. The symptoms subside within 1 week. Six months later, the abdominal pain recurs together with perirectal fistula formation. Colonoscopy shows areas of mucosal edema and ulceration in the transverse colon and rectum, but the mucosa between these affected sites appears normal. Microscopic examination of a biopsy specimen from an ulcerated area shows a patchy acute and chronic inflammatory infiltrate, crypt abscesses, and occasional noncaseating granulomas. Which of the following disease processes best explains these findings?

A 25-year-old man has noted cramping abdominal pain for the past week associated with fever and low-volume diarrhea. On physical examination, there is right lower quadrant tenderness. Bowel sounds are present. His stool is positive for occult blood. A colonoscopy reveals mucosal edema and ulceration in the ascending colon, but the transverse and descending portions of the colon are not affected. A biospy specimen reveals chronic inflammation with non-caseating granulomas. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old man presents with a history of intermittent bloody diarrhea for 3 years. On physical examination, there is no abdominal tenderness or masses. Laboratory studies show no ova or parasites in the stool but it is positive for occult blood. Colonoscopy shows friable, erythematous mucosa with numerous polypoid lesions extending from the rectum to the mid-transverse colon. A biopsy specimen shows acute mucosal inflammation with crypt abscesses and epithelial cell necrosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman has had bloody, mucoid, low-volume diarrhea for the past 7 weeks. She has 5-7 stools per day. She has no other major medical problems. On physical examination there are no lesions palpable on digital rectal examination, and only mucus and blood with few leukocytes are found. Colonoscopy reveals a friable, erythematous mucosa with focal ulceration that extends from the rectum to the sigmoid colon. Biopsies are taken and a representative photo is shown above. Which of the following histologic terms should be used to describe the morphologic changes highlighted by the stars?

A 62-year-old woman with a long history of hypertension is hospitalized with severe congestive heart failure. Several days after admission, she develops abdominal distention followed by diarrhea. On physical examination, she is afebrile. Colonoscopy shows patchy areas of erosion in the ascending and descending colon, some with overlying tan exudate. No polyps or masses are found. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old woman was treated in the hospital for servere bronchopneumonia. She required multiple antibiotics and was intubated and mechanically ventilated. Three weeks after hospitalization, she has abdominal distention. Bowel sounds are absent, and an abdominal radiograph shows dilated loops of small bowel suggestive of ileus. She has a low volume of bloody stool. At laparotomy, a portion of distal ileum and the cecum are resected. The gross appearance of the mucosal surface is shown in the figure above. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her diarrhea?

A 67-year-old woman sees her physician because she has had fever and back pain for the past 2 days. Physical examination reveals tenderness at the right costovertebral angle. Laboratory studies show leukocytosis and pyuria with WBC casts. She has been receiving broad spectrum antibiotics for the past 14 days. She now develops lower abdominal pain and a severe diarrhea. Clostridium difficile toxin is identified in a stool specimen. Which of the following conditions does she most likely have now?

A 19-year-old man experiences cramping abdominal pain with fever and mucinous bloody diarrhea two days after eating an unwashed fresh cucumber when enjoying his summer holiday in a small village. Physical examination shows mild diffuse abdominal pain on palpation, but there are no masses. Bowel sounds are present. He recovers completely within two week after treatment with antibiotics. Which of the following infectious organisms is most likely to have produced these findings?

A 21-year-old man who is enjoying his summer holiday experiences cramping abdominal pain with fever and diarrhea two days after eating contaminated food. Physical examination shows mild diffuse abdominal pain on palpation, but there are no masses. Stool cultrure confirms the present of dysentery bacterium. Which is the most likely morphologic change in his intestine?

A 24-year-old man experiences episodes of abdominal pain with fever and loose stools for nearly 6 months. His temperature is 37.6°C. Radiologic study reveals calcification at the right upper lobe and hilar lymph nodes. Colonoscopy reveals an ileocecal ulcer with stricture. Biopsy from this ulcer shows granulomatous inflammation. Which of the following is true for this patient?

options.A: The major axis of the ulcer is probably parallel with the long axis of the intestine
options.C: The granulomas will be noncaseating granulomas
options.D: The acid-fast staining will be negative
options.E: He should be treated with steroids

questions.title: 31-year-old woman sees her physician after becoming febrile and having pain in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. She reports she previously had diarrhea after she came back from a trip to South East Asia. The diarrheal illness subsided within a couple of weeks. The stools showed mucus and streaks of blood. An abdominal ultrasound scan shows an 8-cm irregular, partly cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe. Which of the following infectious organisms is most likely to produce these findings?

A 36-year-old man works in an epidemiologic laboratory studying infectious agents of the gastrointestinal tract. One day, after doing experimental work, he did not follow the safety rules because he was tired. Two weeks later, he has spiking fevers and crampy abdominal pain with diarrhea. On physical examination his temperature is 38.3, pulse 100/minute, respiratory rate 19/minute, and blood pressure 100/60 mmHg. On palpation, he has an enlarged spleen and diffuse abdominal pain without masses. Laboratory studies show a WBC count of 2330/microliter, Hb 13.8 g/dL, platelet count 280,000/microliter and elevations in serum AST and ALT levels. Which of the following organisms was he most likely using in his experimental work?

A 27-year-old woman sees her physician because of abdominal pain and increasing fatigue that has developed over the past 6 months. On physical examination, her temperature is 36.6°C and she appears pale. On palpation, there is pain in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen but no rebound tenderness. There are no masses, and bowel sounds are active. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 8.6 g/dL, platelet count 275,000/mm^3 and WBC count 6800/mm^3. No lesions are found on upper gastrointestinal endoscopy and colonoscopy. One month later, the patient continues to experience the same abdominal pain. Which of the following is most likely to cause this patient's illness?

A 4 month old male infant is brought to the emergency room by her mother because of severe vomiting. The infant was born at term with no congenital anomalies. His mother has noted marked abdominal enlargement along with infrequent bowel movements for the past week. On physical examination his abdomen is distended but there is no tenderness. A plain film abdominal radiograph reveals marked colonic dilation. A biopsy specimen from the rectum distal to the region of dilation shows an absence of ganglion cells in the muscle wall and submucosa. Which of the following is most likely to produce these findings?

A 60-year-old man has experienced nausea and epigastric pain over the past 3 months. Physical examination is unremarkable. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals a slight elevated submucosal mass with erosions of the overlying mucosa. CT scan confirms the present of a well circumscribed mass within the gastric wall which extends to the serosa. The mass is removed and pathologic examination reveals a spindle cell tumor 8 cm in maximum dimension which is positive for CD117 staining. Which of the following neoplasm does this patient have?

A 50-year-old man has had persistent nausea for 3 years with occasional vomiting. On physical examination there are no abnormal findings. He undergoes an upper GI endoscopy, and a small area of gastric mucosa is noted in the antrum which has loss of rugal folds. Biopsy from this site reveals a monoclonal proliferation of small lymphoid cells. Immunohistochemical stains show these lymphoid cells are of B cell origin. An upper GI endoscopy performed 5 years previously showed gastritis and microscopically there was chronic inflammation with the presence of Helicobacter pylori. Which of the following treatments is most likely to be the best choice for his patient?

A 57-year-old female complaints of pelvic pain accompanied by weight loss of 6 kg over the past 5 months. Ultrasound examination reveals that both ovaries are enlarged. Serologic tests shows a markedly elevated CEA level and mildly elevated CA125 and CA19-9 levels. Exploratory laparotomy is performed. Biopsies are taken from both ovaries and sent for intraoperative analysis. A metastatic signet ring cell carcinoma is revealed on frozen section. Which of the following organs is most likely the site of the primary tumor?

A 55-year-old man has experienced severe epigastric pain, vomiting, and a 10-kg weight loss over the past 3 months. Physical examination reveals fixed left supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy is done and confirms the present of a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. A palliative operation is performed to relieve his symptoms. A 6-cm ulcerative mass is located in the gastric antrum. The tumor has penetrated through the gastric wall is adherent to the transverse colon. The liver appears normal. There are numerous small white nodules on the serosal surface of intestine, spleen and peritoneum. Which of the following conditions may not have occurred in this patient's tumor?

A 60-year-old man has experienced severe nausea, vomiting, and a 5 kg weight loss over the past 3 months. Physical examination is unremarkable. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy is done followed by partial gastrectomy. The gross picture of the tumor is shown above. Which of the following gross types does this tumor belong to?

A 63-year-old man has experienced severe nausea, vomiting, and an 8-kg weight loss over the past 3 months. Physical examination reveals fixed left supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows a 4 cm elevated mass with an irregular central ulceration. The rest of the mucosa appears pale and thin with areas of erythema. Which of the following conditions is this patient most likely to have?

A 50-year-old woman has a 15 year history of chronic atrophic gastritis. She has undergone endoscopic surveillance every 2-3 years. During the last endoscopic examination, a polypoid lesion of less than 1 cm is found on the lesser curvature of the antrum. A biopsy is taken and a partial gastrectomy is performed. Microscopically, it is an adenocarcinoma and is within the mucosa. Which of the following gross types does this tumor likely belong to?

A 60-year-old man has had persistent gastric distention for 5 years with occasional vomiting. On physical examination there are no abnormal findings. He undergoes an upper GI endoscopy followed by partial gastrectomy. Pathologic examination confirms the presence of an early gastric adenocarcinoma. Which of the following conditions will most likely not be seen in this neoplasm?

A 60-year-old man has had anorexia, vomiting, and vague abdominal pain accompanied by weight loss of 10 kg over the past 5 months. Physical examination reveals supraclavicular non-tender lymphadenopathy. He becomes progressively cachectic and dies. At autopsy the stomach is shrunken with thickening of the gastric wall to 1 cm and extensive overlying mucosal erosions. Multiple tan umbilicated masses from 1 to 4 cm in size are scattered over the surface of the liver. Which of the following conditions most likely preceded development of his terminal illness?

options.E: A diet rich in Vitamin C

questions.title: A 62-year-old woman has had nausea, vomiting, and mid-epigastric pain for 6 months. On physical examination, there are no significant findings. An upper gastrointestinal radiographic series shows gastric outlet obstruction. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows a huge ulcerated mass at the antrum. The resection specimen is shown as above. Which of the following neoplasms is most likely to be seen under microscope?

A 55-year-old man has had persistent nausea for 5 years with occasional vomiting. On physical examination there are no abnormal findings. He undergoes an upper GI endoscopy, and a small area of gastric mucosa is noted in the fundus which shows loss of rugal folds. Partial gastrectomy reveals the microscopic change shown above and the lesion is confined to submucosa. An upper GI endoscopy performed 5 years previously showed a pattern of gastritis and microscopically there was chronic inflammation with the presence of Helicobacter pylori. Which of the following interpretations is most applicable to his neoplasm?

options.A: Metastases are limited to regional lymph nodes
options.B: The incidence is high in East Asia
options.C: The 5-year survival rate following resection is <80%
options.D: It has a gross appearance of linitis plastica
options.E: A signet ring cell pattern is seen with light microscopy

questions.title: A 67-year-old woman has experienced severe nausea, vomiting, early satiety, and a 5-kg weight loss over the past 3 months. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows that the entire gastric mucosa is eroded and has an erythematous, cobblestone appearance. Upper gastrointestinal radiographs show that the stomach is small and shrunken with reduced movement. Which of the following is most likely to be present in this patient?

A 38-year-old man has had repeated upper abdominal pain for a half year and it has become worse over the past 2 weeks. On physical examination a stool sample is positive for occult blood. An upper GI endoscopy reveals no esophageal lesions, but there is a solitary 2 cm diameter shallow, sharply demarcated ulceration of the stomach. Which of the following statements regarding this lesion is most appropriate?

options.A: It is probably located in the cardia
options.B: A gastrinoma of the pancreas is probably present
options.C: It is probably associated with increased gastric acid production
options.D: Because of its small size, a biopsy is not necessary

questions.title: A 46-year-old woman is sent to emergency department because of a sudden onset of abdominal pain. She has a long history of heartburn and dyspepsia. On palpation, she has severe mid-epigastric pain with guarding. Bowel sounds are reduced. An abdominal plain film radiograph shows free air under the left side of the diaphragm. The patient is immediately taken to surgery, and a perforated duodenal ulcer is repaired. Which of the following organisms is most likely to have produced these findings?

A 28-year-old taxi driver has had epigastric pain for over 1 year. The pain tends to occur 2 to 3 hours after a meal and is relieved if he takes antacids or eats more food. He smokes and drinks about 150 mL of wine daily. The result of a urea breath test is positive, and a gastric biopsy specimen contains urease. He begins a 2-week course of antibiotics, but on day 7, he feels better and discontinues treatment. Several weeks later, the epigastric pain recurs. If the patient does not seek further treatment, which of the following is he less likely to develop?

A 54-year-old man has had upper abdominal pain accompanied by nausea for 5 months. He has no hematemesis. On physical examination, the stool sample is positive for occult blood. Upper GI endoscopy is performed and gastric biopsies are taken. On microscopic examination the biopsies reveal acute and chronic mucosal inflammation together with the presence of Helicobacter pylori organisms. The presence of these organisms is most likely to be associated with which of the following?

options.D: Development of diffuse large B cell lymphoma

questions.title: A 40-year-old man has complained for 3 months of mid-epigastric pain and nausea. On physical examination he has no abnormal findings. On upper GI endoscopy a solitary sharply demarcated 2 cm shallow gastric antral ulcer is seen. Which of the following is most likely to be present in this man?

A 42-year-old woman has had nausea and epigastirc pain for the past two years. She has been feeling increasingly tired in the recent 6 months. Physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 9.2 g/dL, hematocrit 28.5%, MCV 122 μm^3, platelet count 247,000/mm^3, and WBC count 5500/mm^3. The reticulocyte index is low. Upper GI endoscopy is performed and multiple biopsies are taken. Microscopic examination shows chronic atrophic gastritis in some of the biopsy specimens and silver stains do not show any positive organisms. The biopsies that show atrophic gastritis are most likely taken from which portion of the stomach?

A middle aged man complains for 2 month of gastric distention and vague pain. He has a history of acute gastritis and had a positive urea breath test 4 years ago. His physician suggested he have a course of antibiotic treatment but he did not do so. Physical examination is unremarkable. Upper GI endoscopy shows the antral mucosa is pale，thin and interspersed with erythema. No ulceration or mass is present. A biopsy is taken and a tissue section with a special stain is shown above. Which of the following is correct?

options.B: The purple stain represents intestinal mucin
options.C: The blue stain represents neutral mucin
options.D: It is closely related to Helicobacter pylori infection

questions.title: A middle aged woman has had vague abdominal pain and nausea for the past year. She has tried antacid medications for two weeks with no relief of symptoms. On physical examination there are no abnormal findings. On upper GI endoscopy, the antral mucosal is pale without ulcerations or masses. Biopsies are taken. No autoimmune antibodies are found in serologic tests and a urea breath test is positive. Which of the following microscopic changes is most likely to be present in this woman?

A 44-year-old woman has been feeling increasingly tired for the past 9 months. There are no remarkable findings on physical examination. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 8.5 g/dL, hematocrit 27.1%, MCV 120 μm^3, platelet count 252,000/mm^3, and WBC count 6350/mm^3. The reticulocyte index is low. Antibodies to which of the following are most likely to be found in this patient?

A 45-year-old man has had vague abdominal pain and nausea for the past 2 years. This pain is unrelieved by antacid medications. On physical examination there are no abnormal findings. Upper GI endoscopy reveals antral mucosal erythema, but no ulcerations or masses. Biopsies are taken, and microscopically there is a chronic non-specific gastritis. Which of the following conditions is not likely to be present in this man?

options.D: Increasing risk of developing gastric adenocarcinoma

questions.title: A 65-year-old woman takes large quantities of Aspirin because of chronic arthritis. Recently, she has had epigastric pain with nausea and vomiting and an episode of hematemesis. There are no remarkable findings on physical examination. A gastric biopsy specimen is most likely to show which of the following lesions?

A 45-year-old woman has had nausea and vomiting for several months. On physical examination, there is no abdominal tenderness, and bowel sounds are present. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows erythematous areas of mucosa with thickening of the rugal folds in the gastric antrum. The microscopic appearance of a gastric biopsy specimen with a Steiner silver stain is shown in the preceding figure. Which of the following organisms is most likely to be present on the luminal surface?

A 25-year-old man has an acute onset of nausea and vomiting two hours after drinking one bottle of "二锅头". Physical examination shows no remarkable findings. Endoscopically, diffuse gastric mucosal erythema with focal mucosal erosion and hemorrhage are present. Microscopic examination of gastric biopsy specimens shows increased infiltrates in the lamina propria, consisting predominately of neutrophils. No organisms are found by sliver stain. Laboratory studies show a normal serum gastrin level. Which of the following description is proper for this patient?

options.A: He will recover within days without further treatment
options.B: He will develop chronic gastritis if not treated properly
options.C: The complications of this disease includes pernicious anemia
options.D: Intestinal metaplasia is commonly seen in this disease
options.E: The patient is at risk for developing gastric lymphoma

questions.title: A middle aged man has had difficulty swallowing for the past 8 months and has had a 7-kg weight loss within 3 months. Physical examination reveals fixed supraclavicular lymph nodes. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals an ulcerative mass in the mid-esophagus which almost obstructs the entire lumen. Biopsy is performed and microscopic examination confirms the presence of a squamous cell carcinoma. Which of the following statements is most likely correct?

options.A: The tumor is restricted to the submucosa
options.C: The tumor has metastasized via lymph vessels
options.D: The precursor lesion is Barrett's esophagus with dysplasia

questions.title: A 53-year-old male presents with increasing dysphagia and retrosternal pain. He has also noticed a 7-kg weight loss over the past 3 months. On physical examination, there are no remarkable findings. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals a 4 cm length of narrowing of the mid-esophagus lined by coarse mucosa. Esophagectomy is performed and microscopic examination confirms the presence of an advanced stage carcinoma. Which of the following appropriately describes the gross appearance of this carcinoma?

A 55-year-old man has had dysphagia for 6 months. On physical examination there are no abnormal findings. He undergoes an upper GI endoscopy, and a small shallow ulcer is noted in the middle portion of the esophagus. Biopsies from this area show a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Esophagectomy is performed. The microscopic changes are as shown above and no metastases are found. Which of the following interpretations is most applicable to his neoplasm?

options.A: It has a high potential to metastasize to the liver
options.B: The incidence is high in Western countries
options.D: It is associated with a high fruit diet
options.E: Its precursor lesion is Barrett's esophagus

questions.title: A 58-year-old man has had increasing difficulty swallowing for the past 6 months. He has lost 5 kg in the past 2 months. No abnormal physical examination findings are noted. Upper GI endoscopy reveals a nearly circumferential mass with overlying ulceration in the mid esophageal region. Biopsy of the mass reveals pink polygonal cells with marked hyperchromatism and pleomorphism. Which of the following is the most likely risk factor for development of his disease?

A 50-year-old male farmer from Henan province presents with increasing dysphagia and has noticed a 6 kg weight loss over the past 2 months. His grandfather and father both died in their late 50's with similar symptoms. On physical examination, there are no remarkable findings. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows a 4 cm ulcerative mass in the mid-esophagus that occupies 1/2 of the esophageal lumen. Esophagectomy is performed, and the gross appearance of the lesion is shown in the preceding figure. Which of the following is most likely to be seen on microscopic sections of this mass?

A 58-year-old man has had sour brash and substernal pain after meals for many years. For the past year, he has had increased dysphagia even when drinking liquids. On physical examination, there are no remarkable findings. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows a lower esophageal mass that nearly occludes the lumen of the esophagus. Biopsy of this mass is most likely to show which of the following neoplasms?

options.A: Malignant neoplasm which forms glandular structure
options.B: Malignant neoplasm which is composed of spindle cells
options.E: Malignant neoplasm which has neuroendocrine granules within the cytoplasm

questions.title: A 49-year-old man has complained of "heartburn" after meals for the past decade. There are no remarkable findings on physical examination. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy is performed, and a biopsy specimen is taken above the gastroesophageal junction. Microscopically, the mucosa shows columnar metaplasia with goblet cells. Which of the following description is not correct for this disease?

options.A: It is caused by gastroesophageal reflux
options.B: The diagnosis for this condition is Barrett's esophagus
options.C: The morphologic changes referred to as squamous metaplasia
options.D: The gross appearance of the lesion is usually velvety and erythematous
options.E: The patient is at risk for developing adenocarcinoma

questions.title: A 49-year-old man has had progressive difficulty on swallowing during the past 6 months. No significant findings are observed on physical examination. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows areas of velvety erythematous mucosa above the Z-line. A biopsy specimen from the lower esophagus has the microscopic appearance shown in the preceding figure. Which of the following is the most likely consequence of this disease?

A 57-year-old woman has had burning epigastric pain after meals for more than 1 year. Physical examination shows no abnormal findings. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows an erythematous patch in the lower esophageal mucosa. A biopsy specimen shows basal squamous epithelial hyperplasia, elongation of lamina propria papillae, and scattered intraepithelial neutrophils with some eosinophils. As a consequence of this patient's condition, which of the following complications is not likely to occur?

A 35-year-old woman has experienced "heartburn" and sour regurgitation following meals for the past 2 years. There are no abnormal findings on physical examination. Upper GI endoscopy is performed. There are 2 to 3 cm long tongues of erythematous mucosa extending from the gastroesophageal junction at the Z line upward into the lower esophagus. Biopsies of this region are performed and the microscopic pictures is shown above. Which of the following interpretations is most appropriate for this woman's findings?

options.B: Her risk for squamous cell carcinoma is increased
options.C: Her consumption of alcohol is high
options.E: Formation of a diverticulum may occur

questions.title: A 28-year-old HIV positive woman has had pain on swallowing for the past week. No abnormal physical examination findings are noted. Upper GI endoscopy is performed. There are multiple small ulcers in the lower esophagus. Inclusions are found in the biopsies from these ulcers. She is most likely to have infection with which of the following organisms?

A 16-year-old boy sees the physician because he has had pain for 1 week when he swallows food. Physical examination shows no abnormal findings. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows 0.5- to 0.8-cm mucosal ulcers in the region of the middle to lower esophagus. The shallow ulcers are round, sharply demarcated, and have an erythematous base. The boy has a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia and is receiving chemotherapy. Which of the following is most likely to produce these findings?

An 18-year-old woman has had several episodes of aspiration of food associated with difficulty swallowing during the past year. On auscultation, crackles are heard at the base of the right lung. A barium swallow shows marked esophageal dilation above the level of the lower esophageal sphincter. No myenteric ganglia are present in a biopsy specimen from the lower esophagus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 51-year-old man has a sudden onset of massive emesis of bright red blood. On physical examination, his temperature is 36.9°C, pulse 103/min, respirations 19/min, and blood pressure 85/50 mmHg. Laboratory studies show AST 137 U/L and ALT 108 U/L. The serologic test result for HBsAg is positive. He has had no prior episodes of hematemesis. The hematemesis is most likely to be a consequence of which of the following?

A 35-year-old man experiences a bout of prolonged vomiting, followed by massive hematemesis. On physical examination in the emergency room, he has vital signs of T 36.7°C, P 108, RR 22, and BP 80/40 mmHg. His heart has a regular rate and rhythm with no murmurs and his lungs are clear to auscultation. There is no abdominal tenderness or distension and bowel sounds are present. His stool is negative for occult blood. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
